Where to Stay in Chanthaburi?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Chanthaburi hotels across every budget — from beachfront resorts at Chao Lao and Laem Sing to riverside hotels on the Chanthaburi River, old-town boutiques in the Chanthaboon community and budget stays in town. From roughly ฿450–4,200/night.
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Chanthaburi matter so much?
introHtml: Chanthaburi packs both a coastline and a historic old town into one province, and each area feels completely different. Chao Lao Beach and Laem Sing are the seaside zones, about 30 km from town — perfect for falling asleep to the waves. The Chanthaburi River stretch is a quiet pocket of resorts with pools. The Chanthaboon Riverside Community is the old-town quarter where you can walk to the cathedral and the heritage shophouses. And the town centre is the convenient base near the mall and the gem market. Many travellers book without checking whether they're on the coast or in town, then end up driving 30–40 minutes back and forth every day. This guide rounds up 12 Chanthaburi hotels hand-picked across every tier — each one with real guest-review feedback, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chanthaburi has no metro and no commercial airport — most people drive in from Bangkok in about 3–4 hours, or take a van/coach to the town centre. Hotels here are fairly spread out, so pick by your itinerary: the coast (Chao Lao · Laem Sing) sits 30–40 km from town and is easiest with your own car; the Chanthaburi River is quiet, with resorts and pools, 10–15 minutes' drive into town; the Chanthaboon Riverside Community lets you walk the old town and the cathedral; and the town centre is near Robinson mall, the gem market and the food streets. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Sand Dunes Chaolao Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · Tha Mai · steps to the sea
entries.addr: 73 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Rd, Khlong Khut, Tha Mai, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: At 9.0, Sand Dunes is the most consistently reviewed beachfront resort in this guide — you can walk straight from your room to the sea. Guests love the big sea-facing pool with sunset views, the spacious rooms (almost all with balconies), and kid-friendly touches like the little resort train. It's an easy drive from Bangkok, with plenty of parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, pick the Deluxe Corner Sea View for a direct ocean outlook and a wide balcony — far better value than the garden-view rooms. Book ahead on holidays, as rates climb fast.
pros: Right on Chao Lao Beach — walk straight to the sea
Big sea-facing pool with lovely sunset views
Spacious, clean rooms; almost all have balconies
Kids' activities and mini-train; great for families
cons: The water here isn't as clear as the Andaman side
Crowded on holidays, and rates climb quickly

entries.name: Maneechan Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chanthaburi town · electric tuk-tuk into town
tags: 🌳 Big leafy garden with a pond
entries.storyHtml: Maneechan is a garden resort right in town that scores a strong 9.0 — ideal if you want a restful base but still want to nip into Chanthaburi for food and sights. The draw is the wide, shady garden with a pond, a large pool, and rooms of 40–50 sqm that are bigger than most in-town hotels at this price. There's a sports club, gym, sauna, playground and an electric tuk-tuk shuttle into town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated room set back from the road — it'll be newer and quieter than the older wing. A solid family pick, with a pool and playground on site.
pros: Wide, shady garden with a pond — restful in-town base
Large, clean pool; great for families and kids
Roomy 40–50 sqm rooms, good value vs in-town hotels
Gym, sauna and an electric tuk-tuk shuttle into town
cons: About 30 km from the beaches (Chao Lao / Khung Wiman)
Some buildings are original and look older than new rooms

entries.name: Chaolao Cabana Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · Tha Mai · steps to the sea
entries.addr: 18/1 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Rd, Khlong Khut, Tha Mai, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Chaolao Cabana is the most reviewed resort in this guide — 287 reviews. The standout is the sea-view infinity pool that couples rate highly, plus Pool Access rooms where you step straight from your terrace into the water. With a private beach, mini-golf and a kids' area, it works for couples and families alike, and from ฿1,900 it's good value among beachfront resorts in this stretch.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a sea view, choose Deluxe Sea View or above — the cheaper garden rooms don't see the water. The Pool Access room is the one reviewers recommend most.
pros: Lovely sea-view infinity pool you can actually swim in
Pool Access rooms — step into the pool from your terrace
Private beach, mini-golf and kids' area for families
Good value vs other beachfront resorts in the area
cons: Set away from Chanthaburi town — you'll need to drive
Busy on holidays; the pool and restaurant get full

entries.name: Phuengluang Riverside Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chanthaburi River · Ko Khwang · 10–15 min to town
entries.addr: 8/8 Moo 4, Ko Khwang, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Phuengluang is a riverside hotel that scores a strong 8.8 from just ฿1,100. Guests love the quiet riverside setting with better views than expected, plus an outdoor pool and free kayaks. The Pool Access room and the riverside Jacuzzi suite are photogenic, and the wide free parking suits self-drivers wanting a calm riverside stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick Deluxe River View or above for the water outlook — the cheaper garden rooms don't see the river. The area is quiet, so bring snacks or drive into town for meals.
pros: Quiet riverside setting with better views than expected
Outdoor pool plus free kayaks to paddle
Photogenic Pool Access room and riverside Jacuzzi suite
Wide free parking · great starting price
cons: Garden-view rooms don't see the river — choose carefully
Quiet area with few places to walk to

entries.name: Riverawan Hotel
entries.addr: Soi Rim Nam-Nong Phu Ne Nai, Chanthanimit, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Riverawan is a riverside hotel with newer, clean rooms and villas, scoring 8.6. The highlight is the riverside villas with balconies for watching the sunset, set right on the water, plus a pool and riverside garden that's good for kids. From ฿1,100 for a Pool River Front room, it's good value for a riverside stay with a pool, and parking is free.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Breakfast must be pre-ordered, so sort it at booking. The River Bank Villa sits right on the water and is worth it if you want the full riverside feel.
pros: Newer, clean rooms and villas; comfortable beds
Riverside villas with sunset-view balconies
Pool and riverside garden, good for kids
Good value for a riverside stay with a pool · free parking
cons: A short drive or walk to the old-town quarter
Breakfast isn't a big buffet and must be pre-ordered

entries.name: Kasemsarn Hotel Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old-town centre · walk to Chanthaboon riverside
entries.addr: 98/1 Benchamarachuthit Rd, Wat Mai, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Kasemsarn is the best-value pick for staying in the old town, from just ฿900, scoring 8.4. It sits right in the heart of the old town, within walking distance of the Chanthaboon Riverside Community and the fountain market. It's an older hotel, but the rooms are clean and well kept and staff are happy to recommend sights. Free parking and free Wi-Fi make it a great budget base for exploring the old town on foot.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some Standard rooms don't include breakfast — check at booking, or pick the Deluxe if you want it. The 3-storey building has no lift, so ask for a lower floor if you'd rather not take the stairs.
pros: Heart of the old town — walk to Chanthaboon riverside
Clean, well-kept rooms despite the building's age
Great value · free parking and free Wi-Fi
Friendly staff with good local sightseeing tips
cons: Older building with no lift (3 storeys)
Some Standard rooms don't include breakfast

entries.name: USABAI Riverside Boutique Hotel
entries.storyHtml: USABAI is an in-town riverside boutique with a healthy 250 reviews, scoring 8.4. The draw is its photogenic Contemporary-Chanthaburi design and the riverside corner with a sala by the water. It's in town by the river, within walking distance of the night market and the Chanthaboon Riverside Community. With free parking and an EV charger it suits self-drivers, and it's good value among in-town boutiques.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a river view you'll need a Riverside room — the inner-facing rooms don't see the water. Stroll to the Chanthaboon community in the evening for that old-town atmosphere.
pros: Photogenic Contemporary-Chanthaburi boutique design
Riverside corner and waterside sala set the mood
Free parking and an EV charger on site
Walk to the night market and Chanthaboon community
cons: Inner-facing rooms don't see the river — choose Riverside
Smaller breakfast selection than the big hotels

entries.name: Nisasiri Boutique Resort
entries.badge: 🏖️ On Laem Sing beach · Pool Villa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Laem Sing Beach · Laem Sing · steps to the sea
entries.addr: 105/3-7 Moo 1, Pak Nam Laem Sing, Laem Sing, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Nisasiri is a quiet beachfront boutique resort on Laem Sing beach, scoring 8.4 from 240 reviews. You can walk straight to the sea, and the vibe is restful and low-key rather than busy. Guests love the fresh, well-priced seafood at the resort and the beachside activities — seafood BBQ, kayaks, cycling. There's also a Pool Villa that sleeps up to 8, ideal for big groups or families.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling in a group? Look at the Pool Villa that sleeps up to 8. Ask for a room away from the road, as the Comfort rooms near it catch traffic noise. This is a calm sea, not a white-sand, crystal-water beach.
pros: Right on Laem Sing beach — walk straight to the sea
Fresh, well-priced seafood at the resort
Plenty of beachside activities — BBQ, kayaks, cycling
Pool Villa sleeps several — great for big groups
cons: Far from town — a 30–40 minute drive in
Small pool that runs cool with limited sun

entries.name: K.P. Grand Hotel Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 City centre · next to Robinson mall · near gem market
entries.addr: 35/200-201 Trirat Rd, Chanthanimit, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: K.P. Grand has a great central location, right next to Robinson mall and near the gem market, scoring 8.0. You can walk to the mall, the gem market and the food streets. The plus points are 35 sqm rooms that are bigger than others at this price, plus an on-site pool, gym, sauna and large meeting room. The building has a dated, older style, but it's good value for a central location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a higher-floor city-view room — it's quieter with a better outlook. The decor is older in style; if that's fine by you, the location and room size are great value.
pros: Central location — next to Robinson, walkable sights
Near the gem market, the mall and food streets
35 sqm rooms, bigger than others at this price
On-site pool, gym, sauna and large meeting room
cons: Building and decor are an older, dated style
Some rooms show wear in line with the hotel's age

entries.name: Chernchan Hostel
entries.badge: 🎨 Hip boutique · high score · private rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In town · Chanthanimit · walk to riverside community
entries.addr: 43/11-13 Soi Trirat, Chanthanimit, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Chernchan is a boutique hostel scoring a high 9.0 from just ฿700. Guests rave about how clean it is — both rooms and common areas — the hip styling, and the private rooms with ensuite bathrooms. It's in town within walking distance of the riverside community and the cathedral, with free bikes to explore the old town. Reviews are still few (28), but the score really stands out at this price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a longer stay, skip the windowless Standard and pick the Deluxe Double with a window — it feels far airier. Borrow a free bike and ride through the Chanthaboon community in the morning for a great atmosphere.
pros: Very clean — both rooms and common areas
Hip styling; private rooms come with ensuite bathrooms
Walkable to the riverside community and cathedral
Free bikes to borrow — great for the old town
cons: Cheapest rooms have no window; can feel close over several nights
Still few reviews (28) · the lift is small and tight

entries.name: Eco Inn Lite Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Raksakchamun Rd · city centre · near King Taksin Shrine
entries.addr: Raksakchamun Rd, Wat Mai, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Eco Inn Lite is a central budget hotel from just ฿600 with a healthy 207 reviews, scoring 7.8. It's in the city centre near the King Taksin Shrine and the food streets, within walking distance of restaurants and sights. There's a lift and free parking, and 24-hour check-in — handy for self-drivers who just need a clean, cheap bed. Rooms are small and best for sleeping rather than lingering.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Most rooms don't include breakfast, but you're near plenty of food spots within walking distance. It's better as a one-night stopover than for a long stay.

Has a lift and free parking; easy for self-drivers
Very affordable for a central location
24-hour check-in; friendly staff
cons: Small rooms — better for sleeping than lingering
No pool, and most rooms don't include breakfast

entries.name: Laluna River House
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In the Chanthaboon community · Wat Mai · walk the old town
entries.addr: 192-194 Sukhaphiban Rd, Wat Mai, Mueang Chanthaburi, Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Laluna is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿450, yet it sits right in the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, scoring 7.8. The selling point is the location in a riverside lane in the heart of the old town — walk to the market, restaurants and the cathedral. There's a balcony nook for watching the river, with clean bedding and good air-con. Rooms are small and some have no window, and access by car is tricky (park outside the lane) — but for an old-town location at a budget price, it's a great deal.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Spend a little more on the Superior River View with a window — it feels far airier than the windowless Standard. Car access is hard, so be ready to park outside the lane and walk in.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, from ฿450
In a riverside lane in the heart of the Chanthaboon community
Comfortable beds, clean linens and good air-con
Balcony / nook for watching the river
cons: Very small rooms; some have no window
Tricky car access — park outside the lane

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Chanthaburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay in Chanthaburi — the coast or the town?
faq.a: It depends on your plan. To sleep by the sea, pick Chao Lao Beach (Sand Dunes, Chaolao Cabana) or Laem Sing (Nisasiri), about 30–40 km from town. To explore the old town and the Chanthaboon Riverside Community on foot, choose the town centre (Kasemsarn, USABAI, Laluna, Chernchan). For a quiet riverside stay near town, pick the Chanthaburi River (Phuengluang, Riverawan).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chanthaburi hotels cost?
faq.a: There's a wide range: budget stays and hostels in town start around ฿450–900/night; 3-star riverside hotels and boutiques run roughly ฿1,000–1,800; and 4-star beachfront resorts are about ฿1,900–4,200. Over long weekends and the fruit season, rates can be higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Can I visit Chanthaburi without my own car?
faq.a: Yes, but plan ahead. If you stay in town (near the Chanthaboon riverside community), you can walk the old town easily and get around the centre. But to reach Chao Lao Beach or Laem Sing, 30–40 km away, your own car is much more convenient, as public transport is infrequent. The coastal hotels in particular suit self-drivers.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Chanthaburi hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with each platform's promotions, so it's worth comparing all three before you book — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Chanthaburi?
faq.a: The cool season (Nov–Feb) has the best weather for both beach and town. The fruit season (May–June) is a Chanthaburi highlight — durian, mangosteen and rambutan fill the orchards, with fruit festivals on — but it's busy and rooms fill fast, so book ahead. In the rainy season the sea can be choppier and murkier than usual.

faq.q: ❓ What are Chanthaburi's beaches like — is the water clear?
faq.a: Chanthaburi's beaches (Chao Lao, Laem Sing, Khung Wiman) are on the eastern Gulf of Thailand, so the water isn't as clear as the Andaman side. The appeal is the quiet, restful vibe, falling asleep to the waves, and fresh seafood — more than white sand and crystal water. They suit a relaxed getaway close to Bangkok without a long trip.
